title: Kissena Pond
summary: Kissena is the recorded name for a pond at Flushing in Queens. The source immediately cautions that it is not an original Long Island name, but a later name applied to a body of water now associated with Kissena Park.
address_label: Kissena Lake / Kissena Park, Flushing, Queens, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general point for Kissena Park and Kissena Lake in Flushing, used to orient Tooker's Kissena entry; not an original historical boundary.
history_content: Kissena appears to be a Native-language word introduced from another Algonquian language rather than preserved from a local Long Island source. That distinction matters because Kissena is familiar on today's Queens landscape, but the name is not presented here as a locally documented Long Island placename.
translation_content:
Kissena is traced to Chippewa kissina and translated as "it is cold." The name is best understood as a later applied term, not as a confirmed Matinecock, Munsee, or other local placename for the pond.

Why Place Names Matter

“A name carries history, event, warning, or relation.”

— Sustainable Catalyst, Indigenous Storytelling, Place, and Relational Memory (2026), relational-memory table
land_loss_content: Kissena separates locally documented Native placenames from later naming practices that borrowed Indigenous-language words. The caveat keeps the map useful while making the source history visible.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is a general point for Kissena Park and Kissena Lake in Flushing. It orients the modern place named Kissena and does not mark a Native settlement or historical boundary.
